reviewed_by: Blind MATATAG curriculum reviewer (independent judgment pass, 2026-08-14)

samples_reviewed.question_text: Look at the picture graph. How many are in apples?
Look at the picture graph. How many are in Thursday?
Look at the picture graph. Which has more: dogs or cats?
Look at the picture graph. Which has more: daisies or roses?
Look at the picture graph. How many are in sunflowers?
Look at the picture graph. Which has more: Grade 3 or Grade 6?
Look at the picture graph. Which has more: tennis or soccer?
Look at the picture graph. Which has more: green or red?
Look at the picture graph. Which has more: swimming or volleyball?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every sample interprets an unscaled picture graph, which is precisely what the competency names. Items read a single category, "Look at the picture graph. How many are in apples?", or compare two, "Look at the picture graph. Which has more: dogs or cats?" with the key "dogs". No legend or symbol value is ever mentioned, so the displays stay scale-free as required.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Only two of the interpretive moves are exercised: reading one category's count, "Look at the picture graph. How many are in Thursday?", and choosing the larger of two named categories, "Look at the picture graph. Which has more: green or red?". No sample asks which category has the fewest or least, how many more one category has than another, or how many there are altogether, so part of what interpreting a pictograph normally covers is never touched.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The load matches Grade 1 Quarter 3: counts are read straight off the picture, as in "Look at the picture graph. How many are in sunflowers?" keyed to 10, and every comparison is between just two named categories, as in "Look at the picture graph. Which has more: Grade 3 or Grade 6?". No chained reasoning or arithmetic on graph values is demanded.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Two genuinely distinct question forms appear, and the contexts rotate widely across animals, fruit, flowers, weekdays, colours, sports and grade levels: compare "Look at the picture graph. How many are in apples?" with "Look at the picture graph. Which has more: swimming or volleyball?". No stem is a duplicate of another.

competency_alignment.rationale: Nothing drifts to a later skill, but the comparison items are easier than the competency warrants because they offer options the question never names. "Look at the picture graph. Which has more: daisies or roses?" lists "tulips" and "sunflowers" among the four choices, and "Look at the picture graph. Which has more: tennis or soccer?" lists "basketball" and "volleyball", so in each case two options are eliminable without reading the graph and the item collapses to a two-way choice.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: All quantities are countable one symbol at a time as an unscaled pictograph requires: the largest keyed count is 10 in "Look at the picture graph. How many are in sunflowers?" and the largest option value offered anywhere is 12, both well inside the Grade 1 number range.
